## Purpose

This SOP details the procedures for safely operating the EA Program's
DJI unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for research image
collection. It covers pre-flight setup, flight operations, image
collection, post-flight procedures, and data transfer. Images obtained
from these aircraft are used for photogrammetry (3D modeling), site
monitoring, vegetation mapping, and other remote sensing applications.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All flights of EA Program drones, including the DJI
  Mavic 3 Pro and DJI Matrice 100, for research and instructional
  purposes
- **Does not apply to:** Indoor flights; flights conducted by
  contracted third-party operators; processing of drone imagery
  (photogrammetry, orthomosaic generation) beyond data transfer
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites and approved flying areas


## Definitions

- **UAV:** Unmanned Aerial Vehicle; commonly called a drone
- **UAS:** Unmanned Aircraft System; the drone, remote controller,
  and associated software as a complete system
- **RTH:** Return to Home; an automated function that returns the
  drone to its launch point
- **Gimbal:** The stabilized mount holding the camera, allowing smooth
  image capture during flight
- **Photogrammetry:** The process of creating 3D models or
  georeferenced maps from overlapping aerial photographs
- **AGL:** Above Ground Level; flight altitude measured from the
  ground surface, not sea level
- **VLOS:** Visual Line of Sight; the pilot must be able to see the
  drone at all times without visual aids


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                   |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| PI                | Approve flight plans; ensure FAA compliance      |
| Certified Pilot   | Hold FAA Part 107 certificate (or operate under the Exception for Limited Recreational Operations); conduct flights |
| Visual Observer   | Maintain visual contact with the drone; alert pilot to hazards |
| New Students      | Complete training before any drone operation      |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Rules

- Never fly over people who are not directly participating in the
  operation
- Never fly beyond visual line of sight (VLOS)
- Never fly near other aircraft or in restricted airspace without
  authorization
- Never touch spinning propellers
- Never fly under the influence of alcohol or drugs
:::

### Hazards

- **Physical:** Spinning propellers can cause lacerations. A drone
  falling from altitude can cause blunt force injury. Batteries may
  be hot after flight.
- **Regulatory:** Unauthorized flights can result in FAA fines and
  criminal penalties. See Section 6.
- **Property:** Crashes can damage the drone (replacement cost
  several thousand dollars) and property below.
- **Environmental:** Drones can disturb nesting birds and wildlife.
  Avoid flying near known nesting sites during breeding season.

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (recommended during takeoff and landing)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Closed-toe shoes

### Emergency Procedures

If the drone loses connection or behaves erratically, activate the
RTH function immediately. If RTH fails, allow the drone to execute
its failsafe (automatic landing or hover). Do not attempt to catch a
falling drone. If a crash occurs, document the location and any
property damage, recover the drone, and report the incident to the PI.
Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general
field emergency procedures.


## FAA Regulations

::: {.callout-important}
### Legal Requirement
All drone flights must comply with current FAA regulations. The pilot
is personally responsible for compliance. Ignorance of airspace rules
is not a defense.
:::

### Pilot Certification

Flights for research purposes (not purely recreational) require FAA
Part 107 Remote Pilot certification. The certified pilot must be
present and in command for every flight. If operating under the
recreational exemption (44809), flights must follow community-based
safety guidelines and the pilot must pass TRUST (The Recreational UAS
Safety Test).

### Airspace Authorization

- Flights below 400 feet AGL in uncontrolled (Class G) airspace do
  not require airspace authorization
- Flights in controlled airspace (near airports, in Class B, C, D, or
  E surface areas) require prior LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and
  Notification Capability) authorization or a Part 107 waiver
- Use the FAA B4UFLY app or Aloft (formerly Kittyhawk) to check
  airspace restrictions before every flight
- Pomona College campus is within the surface area of Ontario
  International Airport (KONT) Class C airspace; LAANC authorization
  is required for on-campus or near-campus flights

### Registration

Both EA Program drones are registered with the FAA. The registration
number must be displayed on the aircraft at all times. Registration
numbers are on file with the PI.

### Flight Restrictions

The following restrictions apply to all EA Program flights under
Part 107 unless a waiver has been obtained:

- Maximum altitude: 400 feet AGL (or within 400 feet of a structure)
- Daylight operations only (civil twilight with anti-collision lighting
  is permissible with appropriate equipment)
- Visual line of sight at all times
- Maximum ground speed: 100 mph (rarely relevant for survey work)
- No flights over non-participating persons
- Yield right of way to manned aircraft at all times

| Battery exchange                         | 5 minutes           |

| Post-flight data download                | 10--15 minutes      |


## Procedure

### Pre-Flight Inspection

1. Inspect the airframe for visible damage (cracks, loose components)
2. Inspect propellers for nicks, cracks, or deformation. Replace any
   damaged propellers before flight.
3. Confirm the MicroSD card is inserted and has sufficient free space
4. Confirm all batteries (drone and remote controller) are fully
   charged

### Propeller Installation (Mavic 3 Pro)

1. Unfold the two front arms, then the two rear arms
2. Two propellers are marked (white ring on the center hub); two are
   unmarked
3. Match marked propellers to marked motor joints (white ring);
   unmarked propellers to unmarked joints
4. Press down and twist to lock (clockwise for marked, counter-
   clockwise for unmarked)
5. Verify each propeller is secure by gently pulling upward and
   wiggling

### Camera Preparation

1. Remove the gimbal cover (plastic camera protector) and any gimbal
   clamp
2. Store the cover in the carrying case so it is not lost in the field

### Power On and Controller Connection

1. Place the drone on a flat, level surface (or landing pad)
2. Power on the drone: press the battery button once, then press and
   hold for 2 seconds. The battery indicator LEDs should illuminate.
3. Power on the remote controller using the same press-then-hold
   sequence
4. Unfold the mobile device clamps on the controller; insert your
   mobile device and connect via USB
5. Launch the DJI app. Confirm that the app shows a live camera feed
   and connects to the drone.

### Sensor Calibration

Calibrate the compass and IMU sensors when:

- Flying at a new location for the first time
- The DJI app displays a calibration warning
- The drone has experienced a hard impact

To calibrate, follow the on-screen instructions in the DJI app. This
typically involves rotating the drone 360 degrees horizontally, then
360 degrees vertically. Repeat each rotation until the app confirms
calibration is complete.

### Set Return to Home (RTH)

1. Confirm the RTH point is set to the current takeoff location (the
   DJI app sets this automatically on GPS lock)
2. Set the RTH altitude to at least 150 feet AGL (or higher if tall
   trees or power lines are present). Verify that no obstacles exist
   at the RTH altitude along the return path.
3. The RTH button is located in the upper-left corner of the remote
   controller (marked with an H)

### Weather and Airspace Check

1. Open UAV Forecast and verify:
   - Wind speed below 25 mph (below 15 mph preferred for survey work)
   - No precipitation
   - KP index below 5 (high KP can degrade GPS accuracy)
   - Adequate GPS satellite count (minimum 8)
2. Open B4UFLY or Aloft and verify airspace authorization if in
   controlled airspace
3. Record weather conditions in the flight log

::: {.callout-warning}
### Electromagnetic Interference
UAV Forecast does not detect all sources of electromagnetic
interference (power lines, cell towers, metal structures). Visually
survey the flight area for potential interference sources before
takeoff.
:::

### Flight Operations

1. Announce "Taking off" to all personnel in the area
2. Initiate takeoff via the DJI app or the controller's takeoff
   sequence
3. Hover at 3--5 meters to verify stable flight, proper GPS lock, and
   camera orientation
4. Execute the flight plan:
   - For photogrammetry: use the DJI app's automated waypoint or grid
     flight mode with 70--80% front overlap and 60--70% side overlap
   - For manual survey: fly in a systematic pattern (lawnmower or
     orbital) at the planned altitude
5. Monitor battery level throughout the flight. Begin the return
   sequence when battery reaches 30%. Land immediately if it reaches
   20%.
6. Announce "Landing" to all personnel before descent
7. Land on the landing pad or flat surface

### Battery Management

- One fully charged battery provides approximately 20 minutes of
  flight time (varies with wind, temperature, and payload)
- Carry at least 3 charged batteries per session
- Exchange batteries after each flight; do not drain below 20%
- To remove: power off the drone, press the side release buttons on
  the battery, and slide it out. Handle with care; batteries may be
  warm.
- Store batteries at 40--60% charge if not flying for more than 10
  days

### Image Collection Settings

| Setting               | Recommended Value                    |
|:----------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| Image format          | JPEG + RAW (DNG) for photogrammetry  |
| Photo interval        | 2 seconds (timed shot for grid plans) |
| Resolution            | Maximum available                     |
| White balance         | Sunny (or match conditions)          |
| ISO                   | Auto (100--400 preferred)            |
| Gimbal angle          | Nadir (-90 degrees) for mapping; oblique (-45 degrees) for 3D models |


## Post-Flight Procedures

1. Power off the drone and remote controller
2. Replace the gimbal cover on the camera
3. Fold the arms (rear arms first, then front arms)
4. Remove the MicroSD card: on the Mavic 3, open the small hatch on
   the underside or side of the aircraft and eject the card
5. Transfer images to the lab computer:
   - Insert the MicroSD card into a card reader
   - Create a folder: `Drone_SiteID_YYYYMMDD_AltitudeAGL`
   - Copy all images to the folder
   - Verify the file count matches the number of images taken during
     the flight
6. Format the MicroSD card for the next flight (after confirming the
   backup is complete)
7. Return all equipment to the designated storage location (Mavic to
   SGM 106; Matrice to SGM 210)
8. Complete the flight log entry

### Flight Log

Record the following for every flight:

| Field                | Entry                               |
|:---------------------|:------------------------------------|
| Date                 | YYYY-MM-DD                          |
| Pilot name           |                                     |
| Visual observer name |                                     |
| Aircraft             | Mavic 3 Pro or Matrice 100          |
| Site name            |                                     |
| GPS coordinates      | Launch point                        |
| Airspace class       | G, C, etc.                          |
| LAANC authorization  | Number, or "N/A" for Class G        |
| Flight altitude (AGL)|                                     |
| Number of flights    |                                     |
| Total flight time    |                                     |
| Number of images     |                                     |
| Weather conditions   | Wind, temp, cloud cover             |
| Incidents or notes   |                                     |


## Photogrammetry Processing

::: {.callout-note}
### Software
The EA Program uses [Reality Capture](https://www.capturingreality.com/realitycapture)
(Windows only) or [Pix4D](https://www.pix4d.com/) for generating 3D
models and orthomosaics from drone imagery. Detailed processing
instructions are outside the scope of this SOP. Consult the software
documentation and the PI.
:::

The general workflow:

1. Import all images from a flight session into the photogrammetry
   software
2. Align images (the software matches features across overlapping
   photos)
3. Generate a dense point cloud
4. Build a 3D mesh or digital surface model
5. Export the model or orthomosaic for analysis

For best results, use 100--1000+ overlapping images per site with
consistent lighting conditions.


## Quality Control

- Complete the pre-flight checklist (Section 8) before every flight
- Verify GPS lock (minimum 8 satellites) before takeoff
- After each flight, review a sample of images on the mobile device
  to confirm coverage, focus, and exposure
- Check for gaps in coverage; re-fly any missed areas before leaving
  the site
- Log all flights in the flight log
- Report any incidents (crashes, near-misses, equipment damage) to the
  PI within 24 hours. FAA reporting may be required for incidents
  involving injury or property damage exceeding $500.


## Maintenance

| Task                          | Frequency                               |
|:------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| Visual inspection (airframe, propellers) | Before every flight         |
| Firmware update               | When notified by DJI app                |
| Propeller replacement         | After any damage or every 200 flights   |
| Battery health check          | Monthly (via DJI app diagnostics)       |
| Gimbal inspection             | After any hard landing                  |
| Sensor calibration            | At each new site; after impact          |


## Troubleshooting

| Problem                             | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                      |
|:------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|
| DJI app does not connect to drone   | USB cable loose; app needs update  | Reseat cable; update app and firmware  |
| Compass calibration fails           | Metal or EM interference nearby    | Move to an open area away from vehicles, buildings, and power lines |
| Drone drifts in hover               | GPS signal weak; high winds        | Wait for more satellites; reduce altitude; land if unsafe |
| Camera images blurry                | Gimbal vibration; dirty lens       | Check propeller balance; clean lens    |
| Battery drains rapidly              | Cold temperatures; aged battery    | Warm battery before flight; check battery health in DJI app |
| RTH activates unexpectedly          | Signal lost; low battery failsafe  | Check controller antenna orientation; keep within range |
| "Restricted zone" warning           | Flying in controlled airspace      | Obtain LAANC authorization; move to an approved area |

## Training Record

Before operating any EA Program drone independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) in full
2. Hold a current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot certificate, or have
   passed the TRUST exam (for recreational-only operations under
   direct PI supervision)
3. Complete the DJI app tutorial and demonstrate proficiency with
   simulator mode
4. Demonstrate pre-flight inspection, calibration, takeoff, hover,
   controlled flight pattern, and landing under the supervision of a
   certified pilot
5. Complete at least one supervised photogrammetry data collection
   flight with acceptable image quality and coverage
6. Be signed off by the PI
